subject: Request: Temporary SLA variance for moderation webhook during model rollout
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@brightcommerce.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightcommerce.com
Date: 2027-05-12T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Moderation webhook latency causing structured output failures — request for temporary SLA variance

Hi Laura,

Quick note from BrightCommerce on the rollout this week — we started toggling the new moderation model and are seeing a sharp spike in webhook latencies between our storefront and your content-filtering tool. The symptom is: structured output (JSON schema) occasionally fails to render when the webhook takes >600ms and our frontend rejects the response.

This is blocking a subset of checkout flows (~0.8% of requests, see attached csv). We understand per the current contract the moderation webhook is in the SLO for 200ms tail latency. Given this is during a model rollout and the filter is performing additional content checks, we’d like to request a short, explicit SLA variance:

- Window: 14 days starting 2027-05-13
- Allowed tail latency for moderation webhook tool-calls: 700ms p95 for the window
- Compensating controls: additional monitoring, fallback to cached filter results for repeated users, and increased token-credit if errors exceed threshold

Can you confirm if Redwood can authorize this variance (and if legal needs to sign a short amendment)? Attaching our incident csv for context.

Thanks,
Elena Morris
Head of Integrations, BrightCommerce

Attachments: slo-impact-analysis.csv (CSV, 23KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Morris <elena@brightcommerce.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-12T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Moderation webhook latency causing structured output failures — request for temporary SLA variance

Elena,

Thanks for the data — I reviewed the csv and looped in Diego (runtime) and Marissa (contracts). We can support a temporary variance with conditions so it doesn’t become open-ended. Proposed approach:

- Approve a 14-day variance starting 2027-05-13 where moderation webhook p95 may be up to 700ms for tool-calls originating from BrightCommerce production endpoints.
- We will enable a dedicated routing policy to attempt lower-latency variants first; if those fail, we will route to the tolerant path that allows 700ms.
- Redwood will deliver a monitoring dashboard and daily digest to your SRE during the window.
- If error rate (structured-output parse failures) exceeds 1.5% for more than 6 hours, Redwood must switch to fallback behavior and notify immediately; if that persists beyond 24 hours we revert the variance and engage a hotfix cadence.
- Credit: 10% of monthly hosted fees for time during which structured-output failures exceed threshold.

Marissa, can legal prepare a short two-page amendment to document the variance and credit terms (proposed filename: proposed-amendment-202705.pdf)? Diego, can the runtime team confirm the routing & caching plan and whether we can enforce it by 2027-05-13?

If this looks good, we’ll draft the amendment and route via DocuSign.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

On 2027-05-12 09:03:00 -07:00, Elena Morris wrote:
> Quick note from BrightCommerce on the rollout this week — we started toggling the new moderation model and are seeing a sharp spike in webhook latencies...

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-12T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Moderation webhook latency causing structured output failures — runtime mitigations

Laura / Marissa,

Technical note from runtime: we can put BrightCommerce on a routing policy that prioritizes the quantized filter path and pre-warms KV cache for their top 200 endpoints. Implementation plan:

- 2027-05-12 16:00 PDT: deploy pre-warm job for BrightCommerce keys (non-disruptive).
- 2027-05-13 02:00 PDT: enable tolerant routing policy for their production org id (p95 target 700ms).
- Implement temporary acceptance of partial structured outputs with a signed flag so their frontend can attempt best-effort parse and fallback.

Risks & controls:
- Risk: Increased false negatives while on tolerant path. Mitigation: parallel scoring — we will log both strict and tolerant results and alert on divergence >2%.
- Risk: billing reconciliation for cached/resubmitted tokens. Finance will be looped if credit triggers.

We can deliver dashboards and alerts (internal) by the morning of 2027-05-13. I will also prepare a short runbook for the SREs.

Diego
Senior Runtime Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-snippet.txt (attachment stub)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-13T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Moderation webhook latency causing structured output failures — legal amendment draft

Team,

I drafted the two-page amendment (see attached). Key commercial points:

- Term: variance window 2027-05-13 to 2027-05-26 inclusive.
- Permitted latency: moderation webhook p95 up to 700ms for the window.
- Credit: 10% monthly fee if structured-output parse failures exceed agreed threshold (1.5% for >6 hours).
- Security: Oakridge Security will be able to audit logs upon request; no broader data sharing is required.

Marissa to legal and procurement: please confirm we don’t need additional indemnities. If BrightCommerce signs, we’ll route via DocuSign and create a Jira INF ticket to track telemetry.

Attachments: proposed-amendment-202705.pdf

From: Elena Morris <elena@brightcommerce.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightcommerce.com, Oakridge Security <audits@oakridge-sec.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Moderation webhook latency causing structured output failures — acceptance

Laura,

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we reviewed the amendment and the runtime runbook. BrightCommerce accepts the 14-day variance and the credit terms as drafted. DocuSign has been completed; I attached the signed copy for your records.

Next steps for us:
- Our SRE will watch the dashboard and escalate if parse failures spike.
- Procurement confirms the short amendment in our contract portal.

Thanks for the collaboration — please keep us posted on any hotfix activity.

Best,
Elena Morris
Head of Integrations, BrightCommerce

Attachments: brightcommerce-signed-amendment-docusign.pdf
